claude.note: Written alongside the guidelines by the session that built the set, in three shards; the reference labels, as for U1/U2.

glm.note: Neutral ids (b-NNN) in shuffled order, batches of 20, guidelines plus item text only; map in glm-map.json, raw output in glm-raw/.

gemini.note: Neutral ids (b-NNN) in its own shuffled order, batches of 20, guidelines plus item text only; map in gemini-map.json, raw output in gemini-raw/ (the first attempts that hit the 300 s print timeout are kept in gemini-raw/timeout300/).

normalization: case-insensitive; surrounding backticks and quotes and trailing .,;:!? stripped; one form per annotator per item (first occurrence keeps its type)
gold_rule: a form is gold if at least 2 of the 3 annotators listed it; gold type is the majority type; majority overridden only by an explicit guideline rule
codex_relabel: pending: the Codex blind relabel used for U1/U2 was not run because the user paused Codex; the external blind annotators here are GLM and Gemini
agreement_metric: mention-level micro precision/recall/F1 of the first annotator against the second as reference (F1 is symmetric); span = normalized form match, span_and_type = form and type match; per_type counts only mentions both typed as that type; type agreement is over form-matched mentions
annotator_vs_gold_note: Claude's labels are one of the three votes, so its agreement with the gold is not independent evidence.

overrides.reason: "creates a Store<PluginState>": Store is capitalized mid-sentence where English would not capitalize it, so it is a code type name; Store<PluginState> is a type expression whose names are Store and PluginState. Claude listed Store, GLM listed the whole expression, Gemini only PluginState.
`recall --recall-format context-block ...` is a backticked command line; its command word counts even when it is a plain word (cf. worked example 9, heal).

"reproduce e.exit()": a method called on a local variable keeps the method (rule 3.4, e.exit_code() gives exit_code), and a plain word joined to code syntax is code-marked (render() example). The same item's render, to_string, use_stderr and exit_code are gold; exit is not in the 5.7 generic-name list.
"the Jev-style question framing": label the name inside a hyphenated adjective (SQLite-style gives SQLite). All three annotators labeled Jev in the same construction in u5-137.
"The Jev-style framing": same rule and same case as u5-153.

"heal reports ..." and "So heal --reindex returns ...": heal is one of the guidelines' named plain-word examples, labeled only when code-marked (a backtick span by itself, or joined to code syntax without a space). Neither occurrence is marked, and neither starts a command line (no program, no backticks).
"incl. heal via open_with_all_detected" and "so heal --reindex --dry-run reported": unmarked plain word outside a command line, as in u5-067. The command `axil heal` in the same item stays gold.

type_tiebreaks.reason: "(rg/grep/find/fd/ls/tree)" names the tools in prose: "named in prose, the same tool is project" (guidelines 4).
"via bindgen" refers to the wasmtime::component::bindgen! macro the body names; another project's identifier is code (guidelines 4), as all voters typed it in u5-009 and u5-088.
"the retired macos-13 runner" is a CI runner label, a config identifier like the target triples and feature names the guidelines list under code, not the operating system (macOS).

drops_note: No item was too ambiguous to label.
caveat: The annotators are models, not people; a human spot-check of the disputed items is still recommended before publishing anything.
